newsitem.title: USA: Case Corp sees housing recovery in Australia.
newsitem.headline: Case Corp sees housing recovery in Australia.

text.p: Case Corp, the agricultural and construction machinery maker, said it sees good prospects for growth in its agricultural and construction equipment markets.

Growing demand for grains and other agricultural products, combined with low carryover stocks, is sustaining strong commodity prices, while exceptional harvests in many parts of the world have resulted in more money for farmers to spend on equipment, Case said in a news release.
"We think the fundamentals will remain pretty stable and pretty strong," Case chief executive Jean-Pierre Rosso said in comments to reporters.

Construction equipment demand is being driven by strong housing starts in the United States, and an expected recovery in the Australian housing market, Case said. But the company said weakness could continue in France and Germany if lower interest rates do not generate economic growth.
The company also said it has reduced dealer inventories to about four months, from six to eight months two years ago.
"We're right now at four months in supply and we think we can further reduce that in the next two years," Rosso said.

Case reported earnings of $0.81 a share for the third quarter, compared with $1.19 a share a year ago and above the First Call consensus of $0.78 a share. The 1995 quarter included a $14 million lower tax provision.
Case shares rose 1-1/2 to 49-1/2 a year ago.
